name: Autodesk, Inc.

profile.description: Autodesk, Inc. provides design, engineering, and construction software for architecture, engineering, construction (AEC), product design and manufacturing, and media and entertainment industries worldwide. Key products include AutoCAD, Revit, Fusion 360, and 3ds Max. Under CEO Andrew Anagnost (8+ year tenure), the company completed a transformative shift from perpetual licenses to cloud-based subscriptions, and is now integrating AI across its portfolio through 3D foundation models and agentic AI capabilities.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Autodesk delivered Q4 FY2026 revenue of $1.96B (up 19% YoY), capping full-year FY2026 revenue of approximately $7.5B with billings surging 30% to $7.8B — validating the completed subscription transformation that fundamentally reshaped the business model [1]. Q1 FY2027 continued the momentum with EPS of $2.99, beating estimates by 10.7%. AI Deployment (2/2): CEO Anagnost is deploying AI across the portfolio including 3D foundation models that 'directly reason about geometry and physical relationships,' generative design in Fusion 360, and AI assistants in AutoCAD [2]. Stanford Business School published a case study on Autodesk's AI strategy. 98% of Design & Make industry leaders now use at least one AI tool, with Autodesk positioned as the infrastructure layer. Market Share (2/2): AutoCAD is the global standard for 2D/3D drafting, Revit leads BIM for architecture and engineering, and the platform serves 4M+ subscribers across AEC, manufacturing, and M&E industries [1]. US streaming share gains in AECO and construction validate continued dominance. Pipeline (1/2): FY2027 guidance calls for double-digit growth in revenue and billings with increased operating leverage, and the 3D foundation model platform provides AI capability expansion [1]. However, specific next-gen product launches beyond the AI integration roadmap lack concrete timelines. R&D Intensity (1/1): As an enterprise software company, R&D is the core value driver — substantial investment in AI, cloud platform, and product development across all verticals [2].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Autodesk's mission to help people 'design and make a better world' is specific, thoughtful, and connects design tools to sustainability, construction efficiency, and manufacturing innovation [4]. The mission has shaped strategic decisions — the company powers operations with 100% renewable energy, neutralized GHG emissions through the Autodesk Carbon Fund, and issued a $1B sustainability bond to support eligible projects. It differentiates from generic tech mission statements. Community Impact (1/2): 100% renewable energy operations, carbon-neutral value chain, Autodesk Foundation supporting sustainable design education, and the $1B sustainability bond demonstrate genuine commitment [4]. However, specific charitable program dollar amounts and community impact metrics beyond environmental commitments are limited. Employee Retention (1/2): Glassdoor shows 80% would recommend Autodesk across 4,567+ reviews, with 4.2/5 work-life balance and 4.1/5 culture and values — above average for enterprise software [3]. CEO Anagnost has emphasized that organizational changes are 'not driven by replacing people with AI,' reinforcing that 'humans will always be the most important part of the equation.' Insider Buying (1/2): CEO Anagnost's 8+ year tenure through the painful subscription transition demonstrates conviction. Insider ownership is only 0.15%, but significant equity compensation alignment and long tenure through transformation signal leadership commitment. No notable net insider purchases identified.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. Autodesk's financial profile is exceptional across nearly every dimension. Revenue LTM of $7.51B with the Q4 FY2026 growing 19% and full-year billings surging 30% to $7.8B demonstrate the power of the subscription model [1]. Forward P/E of 15.98 with PEG of 0.80 is attractively valued for a dominant software franchise. ROE of 50.40% reflects outstanding capital efficiency. Profit margin of 19.49% is near the 20% target on a GAAP basis, with non-GAAP operating margin at 38%. D/E of 85% is manageable with $2.92B cash against $2.72B debt (net cash positive). FCF of $2.73B (36.4% FCF margin) validates the subscription economics. 5-year revenue CAGR of approximately 13% reflects consistent compounding including the subscription transition uplift. Altman Z-score of 5.1 is well in the safe zone. Liquidity floor easily cleared: 3.08M avg volume x $205.92 = $634M daily [5].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): Autodesk occupies a complex position — simultaneously deploying AI and exposed to AI disruption. The core professional design workflows (BIM for construction permitting, manufacturing tolerance analysis, regulatory-compliant engineering drawings) have deep moats through regulatory requirements, file format lock-in, and massive switching costs across 4M+ subscribers [2]. However, generative AI poses real substitution risk for simpler design tasks — AI-native tools could bypass AutoCAD for basic drafting, and 48% of Autodesk's own survey respondents said AI would 'destabilize their industry' [2]. CEO Anagnost acknowledged declining employee optimism around AI. The defense is that complex AEC and manufacturing design requires domain-specific AI (Autodesk's 3D foundation models) rather than general-purpose LLMs, but the substitution risk for simpler workflows is genuine and acknowledged by management. AI Opportunity (1/1): Autodesk generates AI-related revenue through generative design in Fusion 360, AI assistants across products, AI-powered sustainability analysis tools, and 3D foundation models — all shipping features integrated into subscriptions generating $7.5B+ annually [1][2].

infinite_game.summary: Autodesk under Anagnost demonstrates strong infinite game characteristics. The subscription transition — abandoning years of profitable perpetual license revenue for the uncertainty of a recurring model — is a canonical example of existential flexibility driven by a genuine cause. The 'design and make a better world' mission shapes strategic decisions (sustainability investments, carbon fund, AI integration), and the willingness to embrace AI disruption rather than resist it shows the adaptability Sinek values. The 8+ year CEO tenure through transformation provides the consistency of purpose that distinguishes infinite players.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Autodesk's purpose to help people 'design and make a better world' connects software tools to tangible outcomes — sustainable buildings, efficient manufacturing, reduced construction waste [4]. This is specific enough to differentiate from generic tech missions and has been partially validated by the subscription transition and sustainability investments (100% renewable energy, $1B sustainability bond, Autodesk Carbon Fund). However, it hasn't survived a leadership transition or existential crisis at the canonical 3/3 standard.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Glassdoor data shows 80% of 4,567+ reviewers would recommend Autodesk, with 4.1/5 culture and values — above average for enterprise software [3]. Anagnost's 'discovery mentality' empowers managers to experiment with AI, and his public stance that AI won't replace people signals organizational trust. However, reviews also cite 'politics and weak leadership' and slow action on underperformers. The organization appears adequately trusting but not exceptionally so.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Autodesk operates in a competitive landscape with Bentley Systems (infrastructure), Dassault Systemes (manufacturing), PTC, and emerging AI-native design startups. Management's decision to embed AI across the portfolio — building 3D foundation models and partnering with AI disruption rather than ignoring it — demonstrates learning from competitive pressure [2]. The Stanford case study explicitly frames Autodesk's AI response as a strategic learning exercise rather than a defensive reaction.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Autodesk's subscription transition is a textbook example of existential flexibility — the company abandoned the profitable perpetual license model that had sustained it for decades, endured years of revenue compression and investor criticism, and emerged with a $7.5B subscription business generating $2.73B in FCF [1]. This was a deliberate, strategically driven transformation in service of long-term relevance — not a desperation pivot. The current AI integration strategy extends this flexibility by proactively incorporating technology that could threaten the traditional business.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): The subscription transition required abandoning profitable perpetual license revenue for years of uncertainty, enduring revenue declines and investor criticism before the model proved out [1]. CEO Anagnost's 8+ year tenure through this transformation, continued aggressive AI investment despite employee anxiety about disruption, and the public acknowledgment that AI will destabilize the industry demonstrate a pattern of choosing the hard right over the easy wrong [2]. The willingness to address declining employee AI optimism publicly — rather than dismissing concerns — shows courage in transparency.

investment_thesis: Autodesk is the dominant design software platform serving architecture, engineering, construction, and manufacturing — delivering Q4 FY2026 revenue of $1.96B (up 19% YoY) with full-year billings of $7.8B (up 30%) and FCF of $2.73B (36.4% margin) [1]. The completed subscription transformation has created a recurring revenue engine with exceptional visibility and expanding margins (non-GAAP operating margin 38%). At 15.98x forward P/E with PEG of 0.80, Autodesk is the most attractively valued dominant software franchise in the market, with 34 analysts rating it 'Strong Buy' and an average price target 55% above current levels [5]. CEO Anagnost's proactive AI strategy — building 3D foundation models that reason about geometry and physical relationships — positions Autodesk to enhance rather than be disrupted by generative AI. The Q1 FY2027 EPS beat of $2.99 vs $2.70 estimates confirms continued momentum, and management guided for double-digit revenue and billings growth for FY2027.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on AI disruption risk, valuation dependence on growth, and GAAP earnings quality. Generative AI poses real substitution risk for simpler design tasks — AI-native tools could bypass AutoCAD for basic drafting, and 48% of Autodesk's own survey respondents believe AI will destabilize their industry [2]. Employee optimism around AI declined 11 points, suggesting internal uncertainty about the transition. GAAP profitability (19.49% margin, $6.85 EPS) significantly lags non-GAAP (38% margin) due to heavy stock-based compensation that dilutes shareholders — insider ownership is only 0.15% despite the SBC expense [5]. The stock has declined 27% over the past 52 weeks to $205.92, potentially reflecting macro concerns about AEC construction slowdowns and tariff-related manufacturing capex reductions. Revenue growth is expected to decelerate from the billing-transition-inflated FY2026 levels, and any miss against double-digit FY2027 guidance could trigger multiple compression from the 30x trailing P/E.
key_catalysts: 3D foundation models and agentic AI capabilities increasing subscription value and enabling pricing power — Autodesk's domain-specific AI moat protects against commoditized general-purpose AI tools
FY2027 double-digit revenue and billings growth guidance with continued margin expansion toward 40%+ non-GAAP operating margins, driven by subscription economics and operating leverage
Free cash flow trajectory toward $3B+ enabling accelerated share buybacks and potential strategic acquisitions in the AEC/manufacturing AI stack
key_risks: Generative AI disruption — AI-native design tools could automate simpler drafting and design tasks, commoditizing portions of Autodesk's core CAD/BIM business as acknowledged by 48% of the company's own survey respondents

Revenue deceleration from billing-transition-inflated FY2026 levels — AEC construction slowdown, tariff-related manufacturing capex reductions, or macro headwinds could compress growth below double-digit guidance

GAAP vs non-GAAP disconnect — profit margin of 19.49% vs 38% non-GAAP operating margin reflects heavy stock-based compensation; insider ownership of only 0.15% despite SBC expense raises alignment concerns
